standard.title: Technical Guidelines for Mobile Access Towers

notes: module_kind = compliance per section 7.12, but the evidence is a CHECKLIST, not a third-party certificate — this is the odd one out of the Phase 3 five. GU74 requires no EIAC (or any) accredited third-party periodic examination. Its recurring obligation is an in-house inspection 'at regular intervals not exceeding seven days', and the only third-party artefact in the document is a one-off product conformity certification to BS EN 1004 held by the tower as supplied, which never expires and is not re-issued. What makes a verdict possible is the set of hard dimensional limits in 4-8 and 4-9 (950 mm guardrail height, 470 mm maximum opening, 150 mm toe board, 600 mm platform width) plus the 7-day inspection cadence — all objectively checkable, none requiring a laboratory or an examiner. Version V 3.0 and issue date 12/09/2025 come from the cover page and footers; note the source URL sits under /uploads/2021/01/ and the catalogue's portal record date is 2026-07-27, so both external dates are wrong and neither was used. Superseded issue date 12/01/2021. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: the scope (p5) cites 'BS EN 1004', the document history log (p2) records an update 'of Standard BS EN1004 to BS EN1004-1', and the References section (p13) cites 'BS EN 1004-2'. Three different designations for the governing product standard in one document; the conformity check cannot be automated until DM clarifies which part applies.

subjects.description: Towers made from prefabricated components in standard configurations to a maximum height of 12 metres indoors and 8 metres outdoors, holding third-party product conformity certification meeting BS EN 1004. Configurations outside BS EN 1004 (cantilevers, towers on stairs, bridging units, linked towers, towers outside the height limits) fall outside this guideline and must be designed to BS 1139-6.
subjects.source_quote: This guideline relates to mobile access towers which are made from prefabricated components in standard configurations to a maximum height of 12 meters indoors and 8 meters outdoors and which have a third-party product conformity certification meeting BS EN 1004 standard.

examinations.cadence_note: 'At regular intervals not exceeding seven days from the last inspection' — a maximum interval expressed in days, not months, and the only recurring examination GU74 imposes. Recorded in cadence_days; cadence_months is deliberately null rather than converted.
examinations.examiner_competence: Not stated for the recurring inspection. GU74 requires inspection 'in accordance with manufacturers' instructions' and names no accreditation body — it does NOT require an EIAC accredited third party, unlike GU48 and GU67. Section 4-2 assigns the pre-assembly component check to 'the competent person' without defining competence.
examinations.source_quote: Mobile access towers are required to be inspected in accordance with manufacturers' instructions to ensure safety. The tower should be inspected during the following: Before being used for the first time; After any alteration or dismantling; After any event which is likely to have affected its strength or stability; and At regular intervals not exceeding seven days from the last inspection

examinations.applies_to: A tower about to be used for the first time
examinations.trigger_event: before being used for the first time
examinations.examiner_competence: Not stated; inspection is in accordance with manufacturers' instructions
examinations.source_quote: The tower should be inspected during the following: Before being used for the first time

examinations.applies_to: A tower that has been altered or dismantled
examinations.examiner_competence: Not stated; inspection is in accordance with manufacturers' instructions

examinations.applies_to: A tower subjected to any event likely to have affected its strength or stability
examinations.trigger_event: after any event likely to have affected the tower's strength or stability
examinations.examiner_competence: Not stated; inspection is in accordance with manufacturers' instructions
examinations.source_quote: After any event which is likely to have affected its strength or stability;

examinations.applies_to: All tower components, checked against the list in the manufacturers' instruction manual, before assembly
examinations.examiner_competence: 'The competent person' — the term is used but not defined in GU74's definitions section, which lists only BS, EN and Manufacturers' Instruction Manual.
examinations.source_quote: Before assembling the tower, the competent person should inspect all the components against those listed in the manufacturers' instruction manual. They should check that all the components are: Present, Undamaged, Functioning correctly, and Be from the same manufacturer. They should specifically check that all castors rotate freely and their brakes function correctly.

examinations.applies_to: The tower as a product: third-party product conformity certification to BS EN 1004. This is a one-off product certificate held by the equipment as supplied, with no stated renewal interval or expiry — architecturally different from the recurring examination certificates in GU48 and GU67.
examinations.cadence_note: No renewal cadence and no expiry stated. Product conformity, not periodic examination.
examinations.examiner_competence: A third party (unnamed; no accreditation body specified) certifying conformity to BS EN 1004
examinations.source_quote: ...and which have a third-party product conformity certification meeting BS EN 1004 standard.

examinations.applies_to: PERSON, not plant: periodical medical surveillance of each employee involved in any work-at-height activity; the employer maintains the Occupational Health Card as advised by the Dubai Health Authority.
examinations.cadence_note: DOCUMENT IS SILENT on the interval. It says 'periodical' and gives no number, and states no validity period for the Occupational Health Card. Both cadence fields are null deliberately.
examinations.examiner_competence: Not stated in GU74; delegated to Dubai Health Authority (DHA) arrangements
examinations.source_quote: The employer shall make arrangements for the periodical medical surveillance of each employee involved in any work at height activity. ... The employer shall maintain the Occupational Health Card as applicable as advised by Dubai Health Authority (DHA).

limits.parameter_label: Top surface of the upper guardrail above platform level
limits.source_quote: Once fitted, there should be no opening in the side protection larger than 470 mm and the top surface of the upper guardrail should be a minimum of 950 mm above the platform level.

limits.parameter_label: Maximum opening in the side protection
limits.source_quote: Once fitted, there should be no opening in the side protection larger than 470 mm... Annex D (p17) repeats: 'If toe boards are not present, the maximum opening must still be no greater than 470mm.'

limits.parameter_label: Toe board height on the working platform
limits.source_quote: The working platform must also be fitted with toe boards which are a minimum of 150 mm high. Intermediate platforms do not normally need toe boards.
Platform units, as stated in BS EN 1004, shall be a minimum of 600 mm wide.

limits.parameter_label: Maximum standard-configuration tower height indoors (scope boundary)
limits.source_quote: This guideline relates to mobile access towers which are made from prefabricated components in standard configurations to a maximum height of 12 meters indoors and 8 meters outdoors

limits.parameter_label: Maximum standard-configuration tower height outdoors (scope boundary)
limits.source_quote: ...to a maximum height of 12 meters indoors and 8 meters outdoors and which have a third-party product conformity certification meeting BS EN 1004 standard.

limits.parameter_label: Tower overall height must be reduced to this figure before the tower is moved
limits.source_quote: Before any movement check: The intended route is clear of obstructions or obstacles at ground level and overhead; The tower is clear of people and materials; Tower overall height is reduced to 4 meters; and Stabilizer should be left fitted to the tower and raised a maximum of 25 millimeters above the ground.

limits.parameter_label: Maximum height the stabiliser may be raised above the ground during tower movement
limits.source_quote: Stabilizer should be left fitted to the tower and raised a maximum of 25 millimeters above the ground.

limits.parameter_label: ADVISORY, NOT A DM LIMIT — wind speed at which work on the tower should cease
limits.display: 27 km/h (manufacturer recommendation, not a DM requirement)
limits.source_quote: It is recommended by many manufacturers that if the wind reaches a speed of 27 kilometers per hour, then all work should cease on the tower.

limits.parameter_label: ADVISORY, NOT A DM LIMIT — wind speed at or above which the tower should be dismantled
limits.display: 64 km/h (conditional advice — 'if there is a possibility of the wind... approaching or more than')
limits.source_quote: If there is a possibility of the wind reaching speeds approaching or more than 64 kilometers per hour, the tower should be dismantled.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum retention period for records of training, induction and toolbox talks
limits.source_quote: Records of any training including induction and tool box talks shall be properly kept for at least five (5) years and be made readily available to Dubai Municipality OHS inspectors and other regulatory agencies for review
